title: Imperfectly Imperfect: Evaluating Graded Cognitive Diversity in LLM Persona Simulations
summary: In the first arXiv version, across seven full-battery simulation runs of four language models compared with 473 adults, simulated agents recovered self-reported trait distributions more closely than cognitive-task performance and downstream behavior. Results show limits of these tested persona simulations, not a general claim about all synthetic populations. The arXiv page states acceptance at NeurIPS 2026; the reviewed source remains a preprint.
ai_technology: Large language models conditioned on cognitive-reflection and personality profiles
organization: University of New South Wales; Aurecon Group

evidence.tested: In four Claude Sonnet 4.6 runs every agent scored full marks on both reflection tests regardless of assigned persona; other runs also overproduced full marks and coded behaviors compared with people.
evidence.unknown: Four models and the reported prompts/tasks were evaluated; results do not establish performance for other models or simulation designs.
evidence.ai_role: Large language models conditioned on cognitive-reflection and personality profiles

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
